claude.sample_unit: de-identified admission notes (each run 3 times per model and condition; 1260 inferences)

links.outcome: Run-to-run stability and parse validity across repeated runs and message-format variation
links.effect: Mistral free-text JSON: 17/70 notes had at least one final failure and 10 had variable status across runs; embedded-user format raised first-attempt invalid outputs 7.9% vs 1.7% (55/700 vs 12/700).
links.quote: The variable outcomes observed for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 under the free-text JSON prompt show that single-run evaluation may underestimate operational instability.

links.outcome: Parse/schema failures with free-text JSON prompt versus schema-enforced structured output
links.effect: Schema enforcement produced 70/70 first-pass valid outputs for all three models in all runs; Mistral final failures fell significantly (p < 0.001) versus 18.6-21.4% persistent failures under free-text.
links.quote: In contrast, under the schema-enforced structured-output condition, all three models produced 70 of 70 first-pass valid and schema-compliant outputs in all three runs.

links.outcome: Omission signals in LLM-edited notes: length ratio, numeric-token loss
links.effect: Numeric-token preservation medians 42.9%, 33.3%, 70.0% under schema enforcement; Llama3-Med42-8B median length ratio 0.81, suggesting omitted content. No clinician adjudication.
links.quote: Llama3-Med42-8B showed a consistent compression tendency, raising the possibility that revised notes may omit content from the original despite instructions not to alter clinical facts.

links.outcome: Model behavior under local deployment conditions and chat-template constraints versus expectations
links.effect: Same-size models differed substantially in structured-output stability under the identical local environment; embedded system instructions increased failures (persistent failure 5.0% vs 0.3%).
links.quote: In this study, all three models were similar in size and were evaluated under the same local environment, yet their structured-output stability and documentation behavior differed substantially.

unlisted_practices: Schema-enforced structured-output (constrained decoding) to guarantee parseable outputs
Placing system instructions in a separate system role rather than embedded in user message
Retry and fallback logic for failed structured outputs
Automated proxy-metric screening before clinician review (staged evaluation)

links.effect: Repeated runs found Mistral free-text variability: 10/70 notes (14.3%) had variable final status and 17/70 (24.3%) had at least one final parse/schema failure.
links.quote: Under the free-text JSON prompt, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 had variable final status across runs for 10 of 70 notes (14.3%), at least one final parse/schema failure for 17 notes (24.3%), and consistent first-pass validity for 50 notes (71.4%).

links.effect: Embedded-user format had 55/700 first-attempt invalid outputs (7.9%) versus 12/700 (1.7%) with separate roles; persistent failures were 35/700 (5.0%) versus 2/700 (0.3%).
links.quote: In the message-format sensitivity analysis, the embedded-user format produced 55 of 700 first-attempt invalid outputs (7.9%), compared with 12 of 700 outputs (1.7%) under the separate-role format.

links.effect: Free-text first-pass validity differed: Mistral 52–55/70 (74.3–78.6%), Llama3-Med42 67–68/70 (95.7–97.1%), Meta-Llama 68–69/70 (97.1–98.6%).
links.quote: Under the free-text JSON prompt, the tested Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3/embedded-prompt configuration showed the weakest structured-output stability, producing first-pass valid and schema-compliant JSON for 52 to 55 of 70 notes per run (74.3–78.6%).

links.effect: Screening identified Mistral free-text failures for 17/70 notes; schema enforcement produced 70/70 first-pass valid outputs in all runs for all three models.
links.quote: Proxy-based screening can identify structurally unstable model-prompt or model-format configurations before clinician review.

links.outcome: numeric content preservation in generated notes
links.effect: Schema-enforced median numeric-token deltas were −5, −8, and −2.5; median numeric-token preservation was 42.9%, 33.3%, and 70.0% by model.
links.quote: In the schema-enforced condition, median numeric-token deltas were −5 for Llama3-Med42-8B, −8 for Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, and −2.5 for Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3.

unlisted_practices: Strict schema-enforced structured-output generation for JSON/schema compliance in clinical LLM pipelines
Automated retry after initial parse/schema failure for structured LLM outputs

links.quote: Under the free-text JSON prompt, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 had variable final status across runs for 10 of 70 notes (14.3%), at least one final parse/schema failure for 17 notes (24.3%), and consistent first-pass validity for 50 notes (71.4%).

unlisted_practices: Schema enforcement (strict JSON schema / constrained decoding) for structured output generation
Prompt message formatting (separating system and user roles vs embedding system instructions in user message)
